This isn't the part two I was talking about in my part one. This is kind of a daily use report. (Read: I still have the stock drip tip.)

I picked up the Erlprinz so I wouldn't have to expose my Squape R to the many and varied dangers gravity has decided it should face lately. I've got the same build and flavor I've had in there the last few days, which might not be the best choice, because I think I still have to mess with the wick a little bit.

My first review might have left the reader with the impression that this is a bad tank, and it certainly is not. I think the airflow caps out at a little under 2mm--just enough to keep me from getting a full lung hit on it. It makes Polar bear seem like a straight menthol with just a little banana when it has a few other flavors going on. It's not muted per se, but it's more that this tank accentuates menthol more than other flavors, and likely accentuates foundational aspects of many other flavors. I know a few atties do this, and I think I'll reserve a post about the ways in which various atomizers work with different components of flavors.

I get some dry hits, but I'm a chain vaper. I think that's why I have to kajigger the wicking a little bit because the juice channels are deep.

Filling this thing is a breeze. unscrew the drip tip some and turn the topmost cap a little to expose a pair of holes. Get your bottle or dropper up against that hole and pour away. If you're a tad shakey like I can be, then you can lock down the cap in place so the holes stay exposed. The only leakage I've experienced is when I tried to fill the tank completely instead of leaving some space, the worst case was a little gurgling when I filled it up like a sensible human being.

I just rewicked the Erlprinz, just to be sure about the flavor. This time the wicks are just resting on the juice channels. It does bring out the fundamentals of the flavor more. The thing that really surprised me with it, though, was the vapor production. This thing really likes to spit out clouds. Relative to the Kayfun before the 4.0, it's not even a question. With airflow the same on the Squape R, same story. Kind of a peculiar quirk, but definitely something to consider if you want more vapor production out of your tank.

In my mind, the biggest competitor to the Erlprinz is the Subtank Mini. I have yet to get my hands on one (I'm waiting for the insulator thing to get sorted out). I think the Subtank Mini is going to beat it on airflow, but flavor is up for grabs.

Would I recommend this so far over a first-gen Kayfun? Probably not, unless flavor and budget don't matter to you. Would I recommend it over a genny style? I'll save that judgment for the post about how atties impact flavor.

So far, 7/10. Totally usable, even enjoyable, but not quite the best out there. It may, however, be the best authentic available for your dollar.

Smart TVs Are a Great Idea. Too Bad TV Makers Are Ruining Them

While I may not fully agree with what he is saying smart anything should be avoided if possible it just a marketing buzzword and adds a operating system ontop of a device which is not needed all of the time.

I don't know if Smart TVs really are a great idea. They, for the most part, just seem unnecessary. Want to stream video? A $50 Blu-ray player will connect you to just about any online streaming service you could want, and many of them even have Plex apps. Hell, you can even play fucking Blu-rays on them too! Average Joe consumer probably already has one of these and can use it comfortably without having any technical knowledge.

Want something a bit more customizable? Streaming sticks/boxes such as Chromecast, Matchstick, Roku, and Apple TV provide a plethora of features for under $100. Hell, even something like the Ouya is pretty decent and will run emulators as well. If a television maker fucks up an update I don't want to be shit out of luck until they fix the problem, I want to still be able to use the television until they get their shit sorted out.

I'm not convinced that the added costs for Smart TVs is at all worth it, especially if you're in a household that has multiple televisions. I just use my computer for media, but my dad has three of the cheapest televisions he could buy throughout the house. He's never going to buy a Smart TV simply because of the cost, but he would definitely buy a few streaming sticks. When I get my Matchstick from the Kickstarter I'm going to let him play around with it, and I bet he'll order a few for himself.
